The image shows a young soybean plant with a neighboring stem that is wilted, brown, and dying. The lower stem of the affected plant appears dark and possibly rotted at the soil line. The leaves are withered and necrotic. This pattern of disease in a seedling, characterized by decay at the soil line leading to wilting and death, is known as "damping off." The description for Damping_Off mentions "rotting and death of seeds and seedlings" and "post-emergence root lesions and discoloration leading to root rot and seedling collapse," which aligns perfectly with the visual evidence.
